final.memo:
We continue to hold our position in the discounted first-lien residential mortgage portfolio. The fundamental thesis remains intact: these seasoned loans, purchased at a discount to par, offer a path to value creation through borrower refinancing and the eventual pull-to-par of principal [D01, D07]. With borrowers maintaining significant equity in their properties—specifically in the 40–55% range—the underlying collateral remains robust despite broader market fluctuations [D02, D03].

While we acknowledge the risks inherent in the credit environment—specifically the potential for financing spreads and interest rates to rise in tandem, which could dampen refinancing activity—our current assessment is that the structural margin of safety is sufficient [D05, D06]. The slight decline in the US 30-year mortgage benchmark rate to 5.98% provides a constructive backdrop for potential pool activity as we look toward the upcoming quarter [D03, D04].

We remain disciplined in our wait for hard evidence. Our next monitoring objective is the receipt of binding term financing and actual cash proceeds from the portfolio, which will serve as the primary validation of the monetization mechanism [D07]. We are not in the business of guessing the exact month of realization, but the portfolio's core descriptors—>18 years of seasoning and owner-occupied status—suggest an investable opportunity that warrants continued patience while the catalyst matures [D03].
